title: Zscaler cloud names: which cloud a tenant is on, and the production name list

prose.text: A Zscaler cloud is a separate deployment that a tenant is provisioned on. {{one-cloud}}

prose.label: What the list is not.
prose.text: Which non-production or government clouds exist, and their names, is open {{gap:non-production-clouds}}. API hosts for government clouds are in [[shared.oneapi.government-clouds]].

checks.do: Read the tenant's Internet & SaaS and Private Access cloud names from Account Settings, or from the admin login host, before naming any host or config.zscaler.com page.
For Client Connector and Cloud & Branch Connector, derive the cloud from the tenant's Internet & SaaS cloud.
If the tenant's cloud is not on the production list, do not reason from the list.

one-cloud.statement: An organization is provisioned on one cloud, and its traffic is processed by that cloud only.

quotes: An organization is provisioned on one cloud and its traffic is processed by that cloud only.
An organization is provisioned on one cloud and its traffic is processed by that cloud only.

where-to-find.statement: The names of the Internet & SaaS (ZIA) and Private Access (ZPA) clouds an organization is provisioned on are shown on the Account Settings page of the Zscaler Admin Console.

quotes: You can find the names of the Internet & SaaS (ZIA) and Private Access (ZPA) clouds on which your organization has been provisioned by accessing the Account Settings page within the Zscaler Admin Console.

name-from-admin-url.statement: The cloud name is also in the URL admins use to log in: an organization that logs in to admin.zscalertwo.net is on zscalertwo.net.

quotes: You can find the name of your cloud in the URL your admins use to log in to the Zscaler service.
if an organization logs in to admin.zscalertwo.net, then that organization's cloud name is zscalertwo.net

when-name-needed.statement: Some configurations require the cloud name, for example SAML for admin Single Sign-On; the name is also needed to find configuration information on config.zscaler.com and maintenance notifications on the Zscaler Trust Portal, and when working with Zscaler Support and account teams.

quotes: For example, you must specify a cloud name when you configure SAML for admin Single Sign-On (SSO).
in order to locate configuration information on config.zscaler.com, maintenance notifications on Zscaler Trust Portal, or when you are working with Zscaler Support and Zscaler Account teams.

zia-zpa-zdx-names.statement: The help lists the production clouds an organization might be provisioned on per service: for Internet & SaaS `zscaler.net`, `zscalerone.net`, `zscalertwo.net`, `zscalerthree.net` and `zscloud.net`; for Private Access `private.zscaler.com` and `zpatwo.net`; for Digital Experience (ZDX) `zdxcloud.net`.

quotes: The following table lists the production clouds your organization might be provisioned on for each service:

derived-names.statement: The Zscaler Client Connector and Cloud & Branch Connector clouds follow the organization's Internet & SaaS cloud: a tenant on `zscaler.net` uses `mobile.zscaler.net` for Client Connector and `connector.zscaler.net` for Cloud & Branch Connector, and each of the five Internet & SaaS clouds has a `mobile.` and a `connector.` counterpart.

quotes: if you are provisioned for zscaler.net for Internet & SaaS, then the cloud for Zscaler Client Connector is mobile.zscaler.net.
if you are provisioned for zscaler.net for Internet & SaaS, then the cloud for Cloud & Branch Connector is connector.zscaler.net.

other-services.statement: The same list gives `goairgap.com` for Zero Trust Branch, `ztsim.com` for Zscaler Cellular, `zscalerrisk.net` for Zscaler Risk360 and `zslogin.net` for the Authentication Service.

non-production-clouds.title: Non-production and government cloud names
non-production-clouds.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "use this as a public production naming map, not as a government-cloud matrix. The list does not by itself identify a tenant's assigned cloud, select an API/SDK/provider endpoint, or establish product availability; retain the relevant tenant configuration and product-specific government-host routing as separate evidence." The captured article lists production clouds only; no captured Help page lists government or other non-production cloud names and how they map per service.
non-production-clouds.blocks: naming hosts, config.zscaler.com pages or endpoints for a tenant on a cloud the production list does not include
